To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2D current density profiles in the BSCO and YBCO tape are different and the residual current flow is asymmetric.
the residual current density distribution of BSCCO tapes is strongly asymmetrical and vortex like, whereas the current distribution of YBCO tapes is symmetric about the center of a tape.
the residual current flow in BSCCO tapes has a strong asymmetry and a vortex-like shape.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the residual current distribution and its dependence on the tape type.
the study of 2D current distribution in BSCCO and in YBCO superconducting tapes.
the 2D distribution of the residual current flow in HTS tapes, which is a crucial issue for the design and operation of HTS devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2D current density profile in the tape depends on the tape material and its fabrication technology.
the 2D profile of residual current density in the BSCO tape is much more complex than that of YBCO tape, which can be attributed to the anisotropy of BSCCO tape.
the residual current distribution in BSCCO tapes is more sensitive to the magnetic field and temperature history of the tape.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 3D Hall probe system and the inverse problem solver are powerful tools for the study of the 2- and 3D current density distribution in the HTS tapes.
the current density profile in the HTS tapes can be calculated with the inverse problem solver based on the measured magnetic flux density.
the current flow distribution in the HTS tapes depends on both the type of superconductor and its microstructure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current flow in the tape after the emergency shutdown is not uniform and is not the same as that in the case of the direct current.
the current density profile is not only a function of the HTS material and tape design but also of the tape history.
the 2D current distribution is a function of the tape type, and the current density profile can be calculated by using a 3D Hall probe system.
